correctness.rationale: For a prescribed final arrival-order permutation pi, before arrival i the vacant set is exactly {pi_i,...,pi_n}. If pi_i is not its maximum then the sole valid request is pi_i; if it is maximum, requests are pi_i plus each earlier occupied lower spot, counted by 1+(pi_i-1)-(n-i)=pi_i-n+i. The allowed preferences vary independently within the fixed vacant-state sequence, yielding the product over right-to-left maxima. If k positions are not right-to-left maxima, a record factor counts at most k earlier occupied smaller nonrecords, so product <=(k+1)^(n-k). Equality at every record requires all k small entries to occur first, with decreasing large suffix; this also establishes precisely k! outcomes for each maximizing k (including possible ties), and the overall maximum follows by finite integer maximization. The known total (2n-1)!! normalizes the probabilities. Independent literal simulation enumerated 50,069 candidate words n<=6 and exactly compared all 873 resulting permutations with formulas and modal counts; universality comes from the predecessor argument.

originality.rationale: Previously published fixed-order fibers under first-vacant-forward parking differ in the rule and use inverse outcome permutations; their consecutive-small-block statistics are not the right-to-left maxima formula for farthest-free frustrated cars. The exact fixed-outcome formula and complete modes do not follow from the published double-factorial total or refinements by lucky sets.
